decisions.context: Weekly store and product demand forecasts need historical data available to repeat past runs. The brief gives no real-time input requirement.

alternatives.label: ETL-based feature ingestion
pros: Reproducibility: batch extracts support repeatable inputs
cons: Weekly run: waits for batch completion

decisions.rationale: Reproducibility decides: ETL fits the stated weekly cadence and avoids adding a streaming freshness requirement. “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” discuss batch ingestion; the checked point has no warnings, though no source attests to the full combination.
consequences: Retain dated input snapshots for past-week reruns.
Forecast data refresh follows the batch schedule.

decisions.context: A weekly end-to-end run must execute consistently, while a three-person team needs to develop and deliver model ideas without relying on manual handoffs.

alternatives.label: Manual script-driven workflow
cons: Weekly run: manual transitions can vary

decisions.rationale: Protecting the weekly run decides: an orchestrated pipeline makes preparation, training, and evaluation repeatable, at the cost of maintaining the workflow. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” support this direction; the checked point has no warnings but is unattested as a complete combination.
consequences: Pipeline changes need review and maintenance.
Model experiments can run through the same stages as weekly production.

decisions.context: Reproducing any past week requires recovering the data, pipeline, dependencies, and model used for its forecast. Model ideas also need comparable experiment records.

alternatives.label: Comprehensive ML lifecycle traceability
pros: Reproducibility: links data, runs, and artifacts
cons: Small team: more metadata to maintain

decisions.rationale: Reproducing past weeks decides: comprehensive traceability includes dataset versions, training runs, artifacts, and deployment status, with higher metadata overhead. “MLOps Principles” and “Continuous Intelligence: Moving Machine Learning Application into Production Reliably” support integrated lifecycle tracking; the checked point has no warnings but is unattested as a complete combination.
consequences: Record input dataset versions, pipeline revisions, dependencies, and model artifacts per run.
Lifecycle metadata adds work to the small team.

decisions.context: New model ideas should reach production quickly, but a bad release must not disrupt the weekly forecast run.

alternatives.label: Progressive release automation with rollback
pros: Weekly run: incremental rollout and rollback
cons: Fast production changes: staged promotion adds steps

alternatives.label: Commit-triggered staged release automation
pros: Fast production changes: commits start delivery
cons: Weekly run: requires effective validation gates

decisions.rationale: Protecting the weekly run decides: progressive rollout with rollback contains release problems, though staging adds steps. “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” and “MLOps: Model management, deployment, and monitoring with Azure Machine Learning” support rollback; the checked point has no warnings but is unattested as a complete combination.
consequences: Keep a known-good model available for restoration.

decisions.context: Model ideas need a repeatable quality gate before promotion so a new model does not degrade weekly forecasts. The brief does not specify a forecast error metric or acceptance threshold.

alternatives.label: Threshold-based quality regression testing
cons: Fast production changes: thresholds need tuning

alternatives.label: Offline evaluation pipeline
pros: Fast production changes: compares candidates before release
cons: Weekly run: alone does not define regression limits

decisions.rationale: Protecting the weekly run decides: explicit quality thresholds can block a degrading candidate, while the specific metric and threshold remain to be established. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “MLOps Principles” describe threshold-based checks; the checked point has no warnings but is unattested as a complete combination.
consequences: Define forecast quality measures and promotion thresholds.
Threshold changes require review as demand patterns change.

uncovered: Forecast error metric, threshold values, and store/product-level acceptance policy.
How source data and labels are retained for historical replay, including correction handling.
Model family, training/update cadence, and forecast-serving or delivery interface.
Monitoring responsibilities and response process when actual demand diverges from forecasts.
